raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies a preassembled, rearrangeable organizer. Its median eleven-minute cycle exceeds the target; five reported component problems and seven of ten unaided customer successes indicate additional gaps, although only two component reports had photographs. D2-O6 limits a blanket account that assembly is inherently too slow: repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, while mixed batches contained every extreme delay. Switching and layout complexity remain confounded. D2-O5 also limits a width-only insertion explanation: measured widths overlapped across first-attempt and repeat-attempt parts. Neither observation identifies a cause or proves that eight minutes is achievable across the accepted order mix.

openings.claim: Switching between layouts may increase selection and checking work, contributing to the mixed-batch delays.
openings.delta: Distinguish configuration switching from the inherent work required by larger layouts before changing the assembly method.
openings.prediction: For the same layouts, both workers spend longer selecting or checking immediately after a layout change than during repeated layouts; insertion time alone does not explain the difference.
openings.probe: Reuse spare-board samples in grouped and alternating sequences with the same layout mix. Counterbalance sequence order across workers, record selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, and audit component counts and colors. Keep the trial within available time before the fixed delivery date.
assumptions: Sample reuse does not materially change fit.
A short trial fits the existing working-time and spending limits.

openings.claim: Does an ordered-layout diagram identifying the short partition improve unaided arrangement when component completeness is independently verified?
openings.delta: Separate difficulty interpreting the generic three-layout diagram from missing parts or physical insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: With complete matched kits, the specific diagram reduces short-partition placement errors and requests for help without changing insertion resistance.
openings.probe: Assign ten participants to balanced groups using the existing or proposed diagram with matched ordered layouts. Record unaided success, placement errors, insertion retries and time. Treat this small trial as directional; cost the diagram substitution against the 500 initial and 0.40 recurring limits before adoption.
assumptions: The diagram accurately represents each supplied layout.
Changing the diagram preserves the specified assortment, footprint, counts, color and detachable partitions.

raw.assessment: Two hypotheses convert assembly friction or configuration mismatch into information. Neither is established by the observations; combined timing and overlapping widths do not identify causes. Product capacity, reversibility, ordered counts and colors, cost ceilings, and delivery date remain binding.

openings.claim: Use first-attempt insertion resistance as a diagnostic signal: stop, record the partition-slot pair and orientation, then test that partition in another compatible slot and another partition in the original slot. Repeated patterns could guide insertion order or orientation instructions without changing components.
openings.delta: A retry becomes information for preventing later retries rather than an unrecorded delay.
openings.prediction: If resistance follows orientation or particular pairings, those patterns recur on repeat trials and the resulting instructions reduce retries on previously untested combinations.
openings.probe: Use spare-board samples to cross-test compatible pairs and orientations at gentle force; time diagnosis separately. Check any inferred instruction on held-out samples. Reject if patterns fail to repeat, handling damages parts, or saved time cannot repay diagnosis before delivery.
assumptions: Trials fit existing time and spending limits; no forced insertions or permanent modification are required.

openings.claim: Turn layout variation into a visible completeness check using reusable order-specific silhouette mats. Place each required partition on its outline before assembly; gaps or overhangs trigger correction. Pair the mat with a matching ordered-layout diagram showing where the short partition belongs.
openings.delta: Configuration differences generate an inspection signal and customer placement cue through one shared part-to-position mapping.
openings.prediction: Controlled omissions or wrong-length substitutions become visible before packing; customers using the matching diagram request less short-partition guidance.
openings.probe: Stage corrected-before-dispatch errors on spare samples, compare mixed-layout task times, and test diagrams with the ten volunteers. Reject if visually identical wrong parts escape, mats mismatch orders, or printing/checking exceeds cost or delivery limits. Pilot success still requires all stated thresholds.
assumptions: Relevant incorrect parts differ visibly in outline.
A reliable mapping from accepted orders to mats can be prepared within the fixed budget and schedule.

openings.discriminator: Switching versus layout complexity or insertion time.
openings.probe: Counterbalance grouped/alternating matched mixes across workers; separately time selection, insertion, checking, packing; audit counts/colors.
openings.uncertainty: Sample reuse may alter fit; trial time/budget unverified.

openings.claim: Order-specific silhouette mats expose mismatch; matching diagrams clarify short-partition placement.
openings.discriminator: Completeness and interpretation are separate effects.
openings.probe: Stage omissions/substitutions, correct before dispatch; compare mixed-layout times. Balance ten participants between diagrams using complete matched kits; record success, errors, retries, time.
openings.uncertainty: Identical outlines evade detection; order mapping can fail. Customer trial is directional; cost printing/checking.

openings.claim: Resistance may reveal pair/orientation patterns useful for insertion instructions.
openings.probe: Gently cross-test spare samples; time diagnosis; validate instructions on held-out combinations. Reject nonrepeatability, damage or no pre-delivery time payback.
openings.uncertainty: Compatible slots and repeatable patterns unverified.

lineage.reason: With A2; diagram effect separately tested.
With Z2; mat detection separately tested.

post_distill.decision: Probe only; causes unproven. Preserve 30x20 cm footprint, assortment, detachable partitions, accepted counts/colors, delivery date; initial cost <=500, recurring addition <=0.40/order. Pilot still requires 60 units: completeness >=98%, median assembly/packing <=8 minutes, unaided arrangement >=90%.
